rules.title: Call first, then build a five-incident log
rules.summary: San Jose prohibits an animal from habitually disturbing any neighborhood or person by howling, barking, crying, baying, or other noise. The ordinance sets no fixed duration or dB threshold. For the city's nuisance-abatement process, Animal Care must assign a case number before you begin, and the signed original nuisance log must document at least five incidents; that five-incident requirement belongs to the complaint process, not the definition of every violation.
rules.captureInstruction: For every incident, record the date, day, start time, end time, duration, source address, and exactly how it obstructed reasonable and comfortable use of your property. Keep a copy; the city form requires your signature under penalty of perjury and submission of the original log.
rules.nextAction: Call San Jose Animal Care at 408-794-7297 during daily field-operation hours, 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.; the city says noisy-animal reports must not use its online animal form. Obtain a case number before logging. After at least five incidents, sign the petition and mail the original to San Jose Animal Care & Services, 2750 Monterey Road, San Jose, CA 95111.

rules.title: Document unreasonable noise and report it live
rules.summary: San Jose prohibits disturbing or unreasonably loud noise that disrupts a neighborhood. Music or instruments violate the rule when disturbing or unreasonably loud to a reasonable person outside the facility or unit where the sound originates; the same outside-listener test applies to shouting, screaming, wailing, and other vocalization. These examples are not exclusive. A loudspeaker or amplifier projecting sound outside a building or outdoors requires a police permit. The code has no fixed citywide dB threshold for ordinary neighborhood noise.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact start and stop times, repetition, where you heard it outside the source facility or unit, and how it disturbed the neighborhood. Note the number of people, dangerous conditions, other possible crimes, and any apparent loudspeaker permit.
rules.nextAction: While the disturbance is happening, call San Jose Police at 408-277-8900 and provide the location and incident details. You may remain anonymous, but the Police Department warns that an officer ordinarily will not respond when the caller is anonymous or unavailable for contact. Call 911 only for imminent danger to life or property.

rules.title: Check the permit and the clock
rules.summary: For construction covered by a development permit or planning approval within 500 feet of a residence, San Jose generally allows work only from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and prohibits it on weekends. An approved permit or planning approval may expressly allow different hours.
rules.captureInstruction: Document the site address, activity, exact start and stop times, day, approximate distance from the nearest residential unit, and the development permit or planning-approval number and posted hours. This citywide section does not decide work farther than 500 feet or work requiring no development permit or planning approval.
rules.nextAction: Check the project's permit or planning approval. If covered work appears outside its approved hours, submit the San Jose Code Enforcement Service Request form. For form questions, call Code Enforcement at 408-535-7770.

rules.title: Check the 30/60-minute barking test
rules.summary: Antioch's current code prohibits allowing a dog's barking, baying, crying, howling, or other noise to disturb a person at any hour for at least 30 continuous minutes, or for at least 60 intermittent minutes during a 24-hour period. It sets no dB threshold. Noise caused by trespassing, threatened trespassing, teasing, or provocation is excluded. The published Animal Services procedure says an initial complaint produces a notice letter and a 15-day follow-up. If the problem continues or increases, an Animal Control Officer conducts a 30-minute sit-and-listen; the procedure calls for an administrative citation when the officer personally observes 30 continuous minutes. If the officer does not observe that, Animal Services may direct the resident to civil court.
rules.captureInstruction: Log the source address and every date, start time, stop time, and duration so the record shows either 30 continuous minutes or 60 intermittent minutes within 24 hours. Describe how the noise disturbed you and any apparent trespass, threat, teasing, or provocation. A complaint must include your name, address, phone number, the address where the dog is kept, and a description of the barking.
rules.nextAction: File the complaint by phone or in person with Antioch Animal Services at 925-779-6989. Keep the barking log after the first complaint. The department accepts another new complaint after 30 calendar days and may use a second sit-and-listen.

rules.title: Document unreasonable noise; no fixed dB cutoff
rules.summary: Antioch has no fixed citywide dB or clock threshold for ordinary neighborhood noise. It prohibits unreasonably loud, disturbing, or unnecessary noise that disturbs the peace, quiet, or comfort of the community or a neighborhood. Listed examples include playing a radio, stereo, phonograph, orchestra, or other musical device in a loud or disturbing manner and continuing a necessary noise longer than necessary. A loudspeaker or amplifier may not project sound outside a building or vehicle except for a public event or dissemination of matters of general public interest, and then only with a permit from the Chief of Police.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, exact start and stop times, repetition, type of sound, background conditions, and how it disturbed the neighborhood. Note whether a loudspeaker or amplifier projected sound outdoors and whether a qualifying public event and police permit were present. A phone dB estimate may support the report, but Antioch's rule supplies no number for the phone to decide.
rules.nextAction: For an active disturbance, call Antioch Police non-emergency dispatch at 925-778-2441 and select option 9. For a non-active written record, use the City's SeeClickFix Private Property Issue category.

rules.title: Identify distance, work type, and any waiver
rules.summary: Antioch has no construction dB threshold in this chapter. Construction audible beyond the parcel, including building, remodeling, demolition, deliveries, powered hammering, sawing, drilling, and testing an alarm or loudspeaker, is limited to 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on weekdays. When the work is within 300 feet of occupied dwelling space, the stricter weekday hours are 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Weekend and holiday hours are 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. at any distance. The same schedules cover starting, warming, idling, or operating grading and earth-moving heavy equipment. Non-powered painting and floor-covering installation are excluded. The City Manager or designee may grant a project-specific waiver, and an authorized employee may issue a stop-work order.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, exact start and stop times, day or holiday, activity and equipment, whether the sound crossed the parcel boundary, and the distance to occupied dwelling space. Photograph any posted permit or waiver and note deliveries, alarm testing, engine warming, or idling. A phone dB estimate does not determine this hours-and-distance rule.
rules.nextAction: Submit the City's SeeClickFix Private Property Issue report. Code Enforcement is 925-779-7042 during business hours; for an active after-hours disturbance, Police non-emergency dispatch is 925-778-2441, option 9.

rules.title: Check persistence, property-line disturbance, and the warning
rules.summary: Oakland prohibits keeping an animal or bird that howls, barks, meows, squawks, or makes other annoying noises continuously or incessantly for an unreasonable period so as to create a noise disturbance across a real-property line. The animal rule has no fixed minute or dB threshold. Noise caused by trespass, threatened trespass, teasing, or provocation is excluded. After an official determines that a Chapter 8.18 violation exists, an investigating official must issue a written or verbal warning; a violation occurs if the disturbance persists for more than 15 minutes after that warning or recurs within one week.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, every exact start and stop time, duration, repeated pattern, and whether the noise was audible across the property line. Note any trespass, threat, teasing, or provocation. Preserve recordings from the affected property. If an official issues a warning, record who issued it and when, then document any persistence beyond 15 minutes or recurrence within one week. A phone dB estimate does not determine this no-fixed-dB animal rule.
rules.nextAction: Call Oakland Animal Control at 510-535-4884; the City's current Animal Ordinance page directs barking and noisy-animal reports to that number. Give the address, dates, durations, property-line impact, and any prior warning. For an aggressive, abused, sick, injured, or neglected animal, the City instead directs residents to Police Dispatch at 510-777-3333.

rules.title: Check character, duration, warning, receiving zone, and ambient sound
rules.summary: Oakland defines annoying noise as repetitive, shrill, or static-like sound, including loud music. Excessive noise is unnecessary noise persisting for at least 10 minutes; an officer need not witness that period when occupants of two or more separate housing or commercial units certify it with particular details. Mechanical or electronic amplification into public streets that produces excessive or annoying noise is prohibited. Separately, persistent raucous or nerve-racking human, animal, or mechanical noise from 9:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. is a nuisance when it disturbs peace or comfort or injures health. After an official determines a Chapter 8.18 violation exists, an official warning is required; a violation occurs if the disturbance persists more than 15 minutes afterward or recurs within one week. Planning Code receiving-property limits also depend on zone, cumulative minutes per hour, day or night, ambient sound, and sound character. Residential/civic levels range from 60/45 dBA for the 20-minute row to 80/65 dBA for the zero-minute row, daytime/nighttime; day is 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. Commercial levels range 65–85 dBA and industrial levels 70–90 dBA. A higher measured ambient level replaces the listed level, and simple tones, speech or music, and recurring impulse noise reduce each listed standard by 5 dBA.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and receiving addresses, receiving-property zone, exact start and stop times, cumulative duration within one hour, sound character, and how it affected peace, comfort, or health. Ask a second affected household or business to keep its own particular log when applicable. Record any official warning and any persistence beyond 15 minutes or recurrence within one week. The code measurement is A-weighted at the receiving property, generally slow response (fast for impulses), with the microphone four to five feet high and, where possible, at least 10 feet from a reflective surface; ambient sound must also be established. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not the complete prescribed test.
rules.nextAction: For an active disturbance, call Oakland Police non-emergency at 510-777-3333, available 24 hours. For ongoing private-property music or equipment noise, file a Code Enforcement property complaint through Oakland's Accela portal. Include the address, duration, affected receiving zone, second-unit evidence if available, and any warning already issued.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Oakland Municipal Code §§8.18.010–8.18.020 and Planning Code §17.120.050

rules.title: Check activity, project duration, receiving zone, permit, and measurement
rules.summary: Oakland has no blanket hours ban for ordinary building construction; sound limits and any project Conditions of Approval control. For construction lasting less than 10 days, Planning Code daytime limits are 80 dBA at residential receiving property and 85 dBA at commercial or industrial receiving property on weekdays 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.; weekend/federal-holiday 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. limits are 65 and 70 dBA. For construction lasting 10 days or more, the corresponding limits are 65/70 dBA on weekdays and 55/60 dBA on weekends. Outside those windows, construction must meet the applicable nighttime receiving-zone table. A higher measured ambient level replaces the listed limit, and simple tones, speech or music, and recurring impulses reduce it by 5 dBA. Grading has separate hours: weekdays 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m., Saturday 8:30 a.m.–6:00 p.m., and none on Sundays or holidays. The City's enforcement page also publishes a residential guideline of 70 dB for no more than five minutes in one hour from 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. Conditions of Approval may be stricter. Engines must be muffled and maintained, unnecessary idling is prohibited, stationary equipment must be placed as far from residences as practical, quiet equipment must be selected where possible, and pile drivers and jackhammers are prohibited Sundays and holidays except emergencies or advance Building Official approval.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit number, posted Conditions of Approval, whether the activity is grading or building, whether the operation lasts under 10 days or at least 10 days, receiving-property zone, exact day and times, equipment, and cumulative duration within one hour. The code measurement is A-weighted at the receiving property, generally slow response (fast for impulses), with the microphone four to five feet high and, where possible, at least 10 feet from reflective surfaces; record ambient sound separately. Also document muffling, idling, equipment placement, and any Sunday/holiday approval. A phone estimate cannot determine this multi-part rule by itself.
rules.nextAction: File the construction-noise complaint through Oakland's exact Accela Code Enforcement form. The City's current complaint line is 510-238-3381. Include the permit or project address, activity type, operation duration, receiving zone, exact times, measurements and ambient method, equipment behavior, and any Conditions of Approval.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Oakland Planning Code §17.120.050 and Municipal Code §8.18.020

rules.title: Separate habitual barking from the nighttime rule
rules.summary: San Mateo's current animal code prohibits allowing an animal to habitually bark, meow, disturb a citizen's peace, or become a public nuisance at any hour. A separate noise rule prohibits unreasonable animal sound between 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. when it disturbs or may disturb a reasonable person in the neighborhood. Neither rule sets a dB threshold. The Police Department's currently hosted 2020 prosecution packet cites the former animal-code section number; its procedure defines a packet incident as barking continuously audible inside your home for at least five minutes and requires eight incidents during one month.
rules.captureInstruction: Record each date, start and stop time, duration, source and affected addresses, audibility from inside your home, and any evidence the animal was not provoked. The hosted prosecution packet also requires two certified-mail courtesy cards documenting eight or more barking days, attempted mediation or arbitration, a signed declaration from you, and at least one neighbor who personally verifies five incidents.
rules.nextAction: Because the hosted packet predates the 2024 animal-code amendment, confirm the current packet procedure with Police Support Services at 650-522-7620 before completing it. The packet instructs residents to retain copies and submit the completed signed originals at the Police Department front counter, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.

rules.title: Check zone, duration, ambient sound, and conduct
rules.summary: San Mateo measures noise on affected property. Base limits are: single-family Zone 1, 60 dB day/50 night; mixed or multifamily Zone 2, 60/55; commercial Zone 3, 65/60; industrial Zone 4, 70 at any time. Day is 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. A source may exceed the applicable base by 5 dB for up to 15 cumulative minutes per hour, 10 dB for up to five minutes, 15 dB for up to one minute, but may never exceed base or measured ambient plus 20 dB. A higher six-minute ambient level replaces the base. Independently of dB, willful loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise disturbing a reasonable person in an adjacent home or business is a nuisance at any hour; additional nighttime music and gathering rules apply 11:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. Amplified-sound equipment is generally limited to 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 10:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Sundays and legal holidays.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, affected property's noise zone, exact times, and cumulative duration within one hour. The code measurement uses a Type 1 precision meter, A-weighted slow maximum, five feet above ground. Ambient is a separate six-minute average at the same location with the source silent. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement. Also document how the noise disturbed an adjacent residence or business and any special-event or exception permit.
rules.nextAction: For an active nuisance noise complaint, call San Mateo Police non-emergency.

rules.title: Check the permit, schedule, equipment, and position
rules.summary: Construction, alteration, repair, or land development authorized by a valid San Mateo permit is generally allowed weekdays 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m., Saturdays 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., and Sundays and holidays noon–4:00 p.m.; the permit may authorize or restrict different hours. During allowed work, the ordinance requires at least one of two 90 dB conditions: no individual equipment above 90 dB at 25 feet, or no project noise above 90 dB outside the project property plane. Pile drivers, steam shovels, pneumatic hammers, derricks, hoists, and similar loud equipment are separately prohibited 7:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. Utilities, street repairs, street sweepers, garbage service, emergencies, and approved exception permits have separate treatment.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit number and posted hours, equipment, exact start and stop times, day or holiday, and whether an exception applies. The code requires a Type 1 precision meter using A-weighted slow maximum, five feet above ground. If safe, document whether a reading was about 25 feet from one machine or outside the project property plane. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement.
rules.nextAction: For active construction or landscape noise, San Mateo directs nuisance calls to Police non-emergency at 650-522-7700. Give the site, permit information, exact time, equipment, measurement position, and any apparent exception.

rules.title: Document habitual, unnecessary, and unreasonable animal noise
rules.summary: Hayward's Animal Control Ordinance makes it unlawful to keep an animal or combination of animals that habitually, unnecessarily, and unreasonably disturbs the peace and quiet of any neighborhood or person by howling, barking, crying, baying, crowing, or other noise. It also declares an animal a public nuisance when it unreasonably disturbs neighborhood peace and comfort or interferes with reasonable and comfortable enjoyment of life or property. The animal rule provides no fixed minute or dB threshold. Hayward recommends first approaching the owner when safe, but Animal Control does not respond to anonymous noisy-animal complaints.
rules.captureInstruction: Keep an incident log with the animal's address, each date, exact start and stop time, duration, type and pattern of noise, whether it was habitual, and exactly how it disturbed peace, quiet, or comfortable use of life or property. Preserve recordings from the affected location and note any apparent outside influence on the animal. Be ready to give Animal Control your name, address, phone number, the animal's address, and the times of the noise. A phone dB estimate does not determine this no-fixed-dB animal rule.
rules.nextAction: Call the Hayward Animal Services Bureau at 510-293-7200. The City's current noisy-animal page requires a nonanonymous report and asks for your contact information, the animal's address, and the noise times. The exact Access Hayward Animal Services topic is also available for a written animal-services request, but the City specifically directs noisy-animal reports to the phone number.

rules.title: Check source property, measurement, reasonable-person factors, and warning
rules.summary: Hayward's dB limits depend on the property producing the noise and the prescribed measurement position. Noise produced on residential property may not exceed 70 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. or 60 dBA from 9:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. at any point outside that source property's plane. On multifamily property, it may not exceed 60 dBA inside another unit on the same property, measured three feet from walls, floor, or ceiling with doors and windows closed. Commercial or industrial source property is limited to 70 dBA outside its property plane, but property abutting residential property uses the residential limits. Public-property noise is generally limited to 60 dBA at 25 feet or more; City activities are exempt. Separately, willfully or negligently producing unreasonable noise at any time violates the ordinance without a meter, based on one or more of 17 factors including audible distance, pitch, unusual nature, rhythm, recurrence, necessity, proximity, affected people, zone, background, time, day, and duration. For a measured dB violation, an officer may warn or cite. For the no-meter test, an officer who perceives a violation may issue a written warning; if a second complaint arrives within 72 hours, signed statements from at least two complainants at different addresses can support a citation.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, source property type, whether commercial or industrial property abuts residential property, exact times, duration, audible distance, pitch, rhythm, recurrence, background, affected people, and effect on quiet enjoyment. For the dB route, the code requires a Type 1 or Type 2 A-weighted meter, slow response except fast for impulse or rapidly varying noise. Outside, the microphone must be at least four feet high, at least 4.5 feet from walls or similar reflectors, and protected from wind and extraneous sound. Inside, average at least three positions, each at least three feet from a wall. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement. Record any written warning and, if noise recurs within 72 hours, obtain separate detailed logs from complainants at different addresses.
rules.nextAction: For an active disturbance, call Hayward Police non-emergency dispatch at 510-293-7000. For an ongoing private-property or city-code noise issue, use the exact Access Hayward topic below or call Code Enforcement at 510-583-4143. Access Hayward is handled during business hours, so include the address, source property type, exact times, measurement method, reasonable-person factors, prior warning, and any second complaint within 72 hours.

rules.title: Check the permit, schedule, equipment limit, and property-plane limit
rules.summary: Unless a duly issued permit or land-use Condition of Approval provides otherwise, Hayward construction, structural alteration or repair, and landscaping between 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Sundays and holidays must satisfy both limits: no individual device or equipment may exceed 83 dBA at 25 feet, and project noise may not exceed 86 dBA anywhere outside the project's property plane. For equipment housed in a structure, the first measurement is outside the structure as close as possible to 25 feet from the equipment. At all other times, the source-property limits in §4-1.03.1 control; work outside the listed window is therefore not an automatic violation. Those limits vary by residential, multifamily, commercial, industrial, public, and residential-abutting property. Alarms and warning devices, emergency response, lawful unamplified events, public-safety audio, and medically required or outage generators have categorical exemptions. A conditional noise permit may temporarily alter requirements for up to six months when immediate compliance remains impractical or unreasonable after available abatement techniques.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit number, posted hours and Conditions of Approval, exact day and start/stop times, whether it is construction, alteration, repair, or landscaping, each device, and the project property plane. If safe, distinguish a reading about 25 feet from one device from a reading outside the property plane. The code requires a Type 1 or Type 2 A-weighted meter, slow response except fast for impulse or rapidly varying noise; exterior microphones must be at least four feet high, 4.5 feet from large reflectors, and protected from wind and extraneous sound. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement. Document any exemption or conditional noise permit.
rules.nextAction: The City's Building Division directs construction-hours concerns to Hayward Police. For active work, call non-emergency dispatch at 510-293-7000. For an ongoing construction project issue, use the exact Access Hayward topic below or call Code Enforcement at 510-583-4143. Include the permit, Conditions of Approval, exact time, equipment, both measurement positions, and any claimed exemption or conditional noise permit.

rules.title: Check the County's 30/60-minute test
rules.summary: Concord refers animal noise to Contra Costa County Animal Services. An animal violates the County rule when its noise disturbs a person and lasts at least 30 continuous minutes, or at least 60 intermittent minutes during a 24-hour period, at any time of day or night. The County rule sets no dB threshold. The initial report may produce a warning letter and a 15-day compliance period. If the disturbance continues after that period, the complainant may file a second report as a notarized sworn affidavit. That affidavit must be submitted no later than 60 days after the initial report and must identify a responsible person; enforcement remains within Animal Services' discretion.
rules.captureInstruction: For the initial report, log the source address, date, every start and stop time, whether the noise was continuous or intermittent, total duration within 24 hours, animal description, and how it disturbed you. Include your name, address, phone number, and the responsible person's identity if known. Only one initial complaint per household is accepted. Continue the log during the compliance period and preserve recordings for a possible affidavit and hearing.
rules.nextAction: Submit the County's initial Noisy Animal Complaint Form. If the 15-day compliance period passes without correction, use the County's sworn-affidavit process within the 60-day deadline. Animal Services can be reached at 925-608-8400.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Contra Costa County Noisy Animal Ordinance Process

rules.title: Document loud and unreasonable noise
rules.summary: Concord directs noise disturbances to Police under California Penal Code section 415(2), which prohibits maliciously and willfully disturbing another person by loud and unreasonable noise. The rule applies at any hour and supplies no fixed dB cutoff. A phone reading may support the circumstances, but it cannot decide the required conduct and reasonableness questions.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, exact start and stop times, repetition, type of sound, background conditions, people affected, and how the noise disturbed them. Preserve audio or video and note any contact with the responsible person or responding officer.
rules.nextAction: For a noise disturbance, call Concord Police non-emergency dispatch at 925-671-3333. The current dispatch page specifically lists noise disturbances as non-emergency calls.

rules.title: Check the district, Sunday actor, and permit
rules.summary: Concord's ordinary construction hours are Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–6:00 p.m. citywide and Saturday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. citywide. Sunday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. applies only in residential districts when the work is by a homeowner, homeowner's contractor, or tenant, and in commercial districts. The code does not give every project a general Sunday window. A use permit, building permit, or environmental mitigation program may impose different hours, and the Building Official may modify permit hours unless an environmental mitigation program restricts them. This rule contains no dB threshold.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, zoning district, exact start and stop times, day, work and equipment, and who is performing Sunday work. Photograph the permit, posted hours, or environmental notice and note any approved after-hours permit. A phone dB estimate does not decide this schedule-and-permit rule.
rules.nextAction: Submit Concord Connect category 'Bldg Const outside allowed Municipal Code days and times.' The Permit Center is 925-671-3107 during business hours. For an active after-hours violation, call Police non-emergency dispatch at 925-671-3333.

rules.title: Check duration, affected homes, and the warning
rules.summary: Berkeley prohibits frequent or long-continued animal noise that causes annoyance or discomfort to two or more reasonable people of normal sensitivity living in separate residences. The City may proceed on one person's complaint when the circumstances show that only one individual is affected. Noise audible continuously for 10 minutes or intermittently for 30 minutes is prima facie evidence, meaning sufficient initial evidence rather than the only possible proof; pitch, pattern, and frequency also matter. There is no dB threshold. A City Noise Control Officer or Animal Control Officer must first issue a warning. A violation arises if the noise persists after that warning or recurs within eight hours.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the animal and source address, every start and stop time, continuous and intermittent totals, pitch, pattern, frequency, and how each affected household was disturbed. Identify complainants by separate residence. Record when the City issued its warning and whether the noise persisted or recurred within eight hours.
rules.nextAction: Berkeley directs excessive animal noise to Animal Care Services at 510-981-6600. Ask that the complaint and required warning be documented.

rules.title: Identify receiving zone, duration, and City procedure
rules.summary: For sound measured on another property, Berkeley's exterior base limits are R-1/R-2 and related low-density residential zones 55 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. and 45 at night; R-3 and denser residential 60/55; commercial 65/60; and industrial 70 at any time. The base may be exceeded by 5 dBA for no more than 15 cumulative minutes per hour, 10 dBA for no more than five minutes, 15 dBA for no more than one minute, and 20 dBA for no period. A higher measured ambient level replaces the base. Inside neighboring multifamily units the limits are 45 dBA day/40 night, with separate five-minute, one-minute, and any-time steps. Radios, televisions, instruments, and loudspeakers violate the specific rule only after both the City's warning and prescribed measurement procedures; a permitted variance may authorize sound. A separate reasonable-person rule covers loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and receiving addresses, receiving property's zoning, whether the measurement point is outdoors on the receiver's property or inside a neighboring multifamily unit, exact times, and cumulative duration within one hour. The City measurement uses A-weighting and slow response on the receiver's property. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not the prescribed City measurement. Record any permit or variance, the City warning, and whether the sound persisted or recurred within eight hours. The investigation procedure calls for one non-anonymous complaint except in a commercial area or for an event, where it calls for two.
rules.nextAction: Submit the City's online Miscellaneous Internet Request for a formal noise report. Environmental Health is 510-981-5310. If the disturbance requires immediate police response, call 510-981-5900.

rules.title: Check hours, receiving zone, equipment, and duration
rules.summary: Berkeley construction before 7:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m. on weekdays, or before 9:00 a.m. or after 8:00 p.m. on weekends and holidays, violates the construction rule when sound crossing a residential or commercial property line also exceeds the applicable exterior or interior standard; the hours alone are not the complete legal test. Emergency utility work and an Environmental Health variance are exceptions. Where technically and economically feasible during the listed hours, short-term mobile equipment used for fewer than 10 days is limited at affected R-1/R-2, R-3-and-denser, and commercial/industrial properties to 75/80/85 dBA on weekdays and 60/65/70 on weekends and holidays. Repetitively scheduled stationary equipment used for 10 days or more is limited to 60/65/70 on weekdays and 50/55/60 on weekends and holidays. The City's warning and prescribed measurement procedures must both occur before a construction-noise violation arises.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project and receiving addresses, exact start and stop times, day or holiday, receiving zone, equipment, and whether it is mobile work lasting fewer than 10 days or stationary/repetitive work lasting at least 10 days. Record sound crossing the property line, cumulative duration, any permit, variance, or emergency utility work, the City warning, and whether noise persisted or recurred within eight hours. The City uses A-weighted slow measurements on the receiver's property; a phone estimate is supporting evidence only.
rules.nextAction: Submit the City's online Miscellaneous Internet Request for construction noise. Environmental Health is 510-981-5310. If an active disturbance requires immediate police response, call 510-981-5900.

rules.title: Apply the unreasonable-period rule and complete the two-week journal
rules.summary: Vallejo prohibits allowing an animal or bird to howl, bark, meow, squawk, or make other annoying noise continuously or incessantly for an unreasonable period so as to create a noise disturbance across a residential real-property line. The ordinance supplies no fixed minute or dB threshold. Noise caused by trespass, threatened trespass, teasing, or provocation is excluded, and zoos and animal theme parks are exempt. Enforcement may proceed without a warning. If an officer instead gives a written or verbal warning, persistence for more than five minutes afterward or recurrence within one week may lead to a citation. The City's current Animal Control instructions require a two-week barking journal recording the days, times, and description of the dog.
rules.captureInstruction: For two full weeks, record the animal and source address, dog description, every date, exact start and stop time, duration, pattern, and whether the noise crossed a residential property line. Describe the disturbance to a reasonable person and note any trespass, threat, teasing, or provocation. Preserve recordings from the affected property. Record any official warning and any persistence beyond five minutes or recurrence within one week. A phone dB estimate does not determine this no-fixed-dB rule.
rules.nextAction: After preparing the two-week journal, call Solano County Sheriff's Animal Control Dispatch. On weekdays call 707-784-4733 and select option 2; on weekends call 707-421-7090. Routine non-emergency information may also be emailed to SheriffACO@solanocounty.com. Give the animal description, address, complete journal, property-line impact, and any warning.

rules.title: Check reasonable-person factors, regular-use limits, and any warning
rules.summary: Vallejo prohibits willfully making or continuing loud, unnecessary, and unusual noise that disturbs neighborhood peace or causes discomfort or annoyance to a reasonable person. The City considers level, usual or unusual character, natural or unnatural origin, background, proximity to sleeping facilities, zone, density, time, duration, recurrence, and commercial or noncommercial source. Amplifying sound into public streets so as to cause a noise disturbance is separately prohibited. Enforcement may proceed without a warning. If an officer uses an intermediate written or verbal warning, persistence for more than five minutes afterward or recurrence within one week may lead to a citation. For regularly occurring noise averaged over an hour, the Zoning Code also applies zone-based limits. Levels that may not be exceeded for more than 30 minutes per hour are: single-unit residential 60 dBA; multiple-unit residential 65; commercial, mixed-use, medical, and office 70 at the source boundary and 60 at a residential-zone boundary; light and general industrial 75 at the source or district boundary and 65 at a residential-zone boundary; and public, community, open-space, and recreation uses 65 at their boundary and 60 at a residential-zone boundary. From 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., nonresidential sources at a residential-zone boundary are limited to 50 dBA or ambient for the five-minute row; residential-zone source limits are reduced by 10 dBA. Incidental, infrequent, or unexpected noise remains governed by Chapter 7.84, and the more restrictive applicable rule controls.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, source zoning district, residential boundary if any, exact times, cumulative minutes in one hour, recurrence, background, affected sleeping facilities, and reasonable-person impact. Record any official warning and persistence beyond five minutes or recurrence within one week. Zoning-Code measurement uses an approximately calibrated A-weighted meter, slow response except fast for sounds lasting two seconds or less, at the applicable lot or district line. The microphone must be at least four feet high, at least four feet from large reflecting surfaces, protected from wind, and never within five feet of the source; the reported level is averaged over one hour. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement.
rules.nextAction: For an active disturbance, call Vallejo Police non-emergency at 707-648-4321. For a written or recurring complaint, the City directs noise reports to Code Enforcement at 707-648-4469, CodeEnforcement@cityofvallejo.net, or SeeClickFix. The live portal currently has no dedicated Noise category, so the exact button below opens its active Other ticket; begin the description with "Noise Complaint" and include the address, legal test, logs, measurements, and warning history.

rules.title: Check operation type, zone, duration, permit, schedule, and measurement
rules.summary: Vallejo applies several construction tests. Grading and pile driving within one-quarter mile of residential units are limited to weekdays 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., unless an approval is more restrictive. Construction, demolition, and related loading or unloading in residential or mixed-use districts that may exceed the temporary-construction table are limited to 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. Temporary mobile equipment used intermittently for less than 15 days is limited on weekdays 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. to 75 dBA in RR/RLD zones, 80 in RMD/RHD/NMX/NC zones, and 85 in commercial or industrial zones; Saturday 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. limits are 60/65/70 dBA, with no Sunday or legal-holiday table allowance. Stationary-equipment limits are 60/65/70 dBA on weekdays and Saturdays during those table hours, with no Sunday or legal-holiday allowance. A permit or variance may impose stricter hours. Separately, Chapter 7.84 prohibits noisy building-material handling and mechanically powered saws, drills, sanders, grinders, and similar tools from 9:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. when sound crosses a residential boundary. Public-entity activities are exempt from Chapter 7.84, and garbage and recycling franchises are exempt from its loading rule. Enforcement under Chapter 7.84 may proceed without a warning; if a warning is used, persistence beyond five minutes or recurrence within one week may lead to citation.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit and conditions, source and receiving zones, distance to residential units, whether the work is grading, pile driving, loading, mobile short-term equipment, or stationary equipment, whether mobile work will last under 15 days, exact day and start/stop times, cumulative operation, and any exception. Zoning-Code measurement uses an approximately calibrated A-weighted meter, slow response except fast for sounds lasting two seconds or less, at the applicable lot or district line. The microphone must be at least four feet high, at least four feet from reflecting surfaces, protected from wind, and never within five feet of the source; the reported level is averaged over one hour. A phone estimate cannot decide this multi-part rule by itself. Record any official warning and what happened during the following five minutes and week.
rules.nextAction: Submit a written construction-noise report to Code Enforcement. The live SeeClickFix portal has no dedicated Noise category, so the exact button opens its active Other ticket; begin with "Construction Noise Complaint." Code Enforcement is 707-648-4469 and CodeEnforcement@cityofvallejo.net. For active after-hours noise, call Vallejo Police non-emergency at 707-648-4321.

rules.title: Separate Richmond's city rule from the County complaint threshold
rules.summary: Richmond prohibits keeping an animal or bird that howls, barks, meows, squawks, or makes other annoying noise continuously or incessantly for an unreasonable period so as to create a noise disturbance across a real-property line. The City rule has no fixed minute or dB threshold. Noise caused by trespass, threatened trespass, teasing, or provocation is excluded; public zoos, licensed animal parks, and licensed veterinary facilities are exempt. After an official determines that a fixed-location City violation exists, an investigating officer must issue a written or verbal warning; a City violation occurs if the disturbance persists for more than five minutes afterward or recurs within 90 days. Separately, Contra Costa County Animal Services accepts its administrative noisy-animal complaint when disturbing noise lasts at least 30 continuous minutes or 60 intermittent minutes in 24 hours. Its process may send a warning letter with a 15-day compliance period, followed by a notarized sworn affidavit due no later than 60 days after the initial report. Missing the County's 30/60 intake threshold does not establish compliance with Richmond's separate no-fixed-minute City rule.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the animal and source address, every date, exact start and stop time, continuous and intermittent totals within 24 hours, repeated pattern, property-line audibility, disturbance, and any trespass, threat, teasing, or provocation. Preserve recordings. For the City path, record the officer's warning and any persistence beyond five minutes or recurrence within 90 days. For the County path, identify the responsible person, continue logging through the 15-day period, and preserve evidence for a possible notarized affidavit and hearing. A phone dB estimate does not determine the City animal rule.
rules.nextAction: For the County administrative process, submit the initial Noisy Animal Complaint Form. If the disturbance continues after the 15-day compliance period, follow the County's sworn-affidavit procedure within 60 days. For an active Richmond city-ordinance violation, call Richmond Police non-emergency at 510-233-1214. Contra Costa County Animal Services is 925-608-8400.

rules.title: Check disturbance, duration, warning, officer-selected test, zone, and measurement
rules.summary: Richmond prohibits loud, raucous, unnecessary, and unusual noise that disturbs neighborhood peace or annoys a reasonable person, and specifically prohibits operating radios, stereos, drums, musical instruments, or similar devices so as to create a noise disturbance. Annoying noise includes repetitive, shrill, or static-like sound. Excessive noise means unnecessary noise lasting at least 10 minutes; an officer need not witness that period if occupants of two or more separate housing or commercial units certify it with particular details. The City also considers volume, background, proximity, zone, density, time, duration, recurrence, commercial character, audibility more than 25 feet beyond an adjoining residential property boundary, intrusiveness, mobility, and people affected. After an official determines that a fixed-location violation exists, an official warning is required; a violation occurs if the disturbance persists for more than five minutes afterward or recurs within 90 days. An enforcing officer may instead choose the §9.52.100 dBA test as the sole test for that incident. Its 30-minute-per-hour source-boundary levels are 60 dBA single-family residential, 65 multifamily, 70 commercial and light-industrial/office-flex, 75 heavy/marine industrial, and 65 public/community/open/recreation. At residential-zone boundaries, commercial and light-industrial/office-flex sources use 60, heavy/marine industrial 65, and public/community/open/recreation 60. From 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., those nonresidential sources at a residential boundary use 50 dBA or ambient for the five-minute row; residential-zone source limits fall 10 dBA. Pure tones, impulses, music, or speech reduce the levels by 5 dBA. Separately, the current Zoning Code applies receiving-zone, duration, interior, and ambient limits to regularly occurring noise; incidental or unexpected noise and unamplified voices remain under Chapter 9.52, and the more restrictive applicable rule controls.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, source and receiving zones, exact start and stop times, cumulative minutes per hour, audibility distance, character, recurrence, background, people affected, and reasonable-person impact. Ask a second affected household or business to keep a separate detailed log when applicable. Record the official warning and any persistence beyond five minutes or recurrence within 90 days. If an officer chooses the dBA test, a defense reading must match the exact time, location, weather, and other conditions and come from a currently calibrated meter with proof of the operator's training or expertise. Zoning measurements use an ANSI sound meter, A-weighting, a calibration check, exterior lot-line measurement, or the center of an affected habitable room five feet above the floor for interior measurement. A phone estimate cannot pass or fail these requirements by itself.
rules.nextAction: For an active loud-noise or music complaint, call Richmond Police non-emergency at 510-233-1214; the City's current Communications Center specifically lists loud noise and music. For a recurring property-based code complaint, use the City's current iMS complaint system or call Code Enforcement at 510-621-1279. Include the address, legal route, logs, zone, measurement method, warning time, and recurrence.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Richmond Municipal Code Chapter 9.52 and Article 15.04.605

rules.title: Check project type, waiver, conditions, schedule, equipment class, zone, and warning
rules.summary: Richmond's current Zoning Code limits general construction noise to weekdays 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. and pile driving or similarly loud activity to weekdays 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. General noise-producing construction is not allowed on Sundays or federal holidays without a temporary Building Official waiver. A specific exception for projects repairing, renovating, or adding to residential structures with one to five dwelling units allows 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Monday–Friday and 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Saturdays, Sundays, and federal holidays. Preconstruction loading, toilet servicing, deliveries, truck idling, backup beeps, yelling, and radios share the applicable construction hours. Permit conditions may be more restrictive; emergency and specified public-works activity have exceptions. Where technically and economically feasible, Chapter 9.52 also limits mobile intermittent equipment used for less than 15 days to 75/80/85 dBA at affected single-family/multifamily/commercial-industrial property on weekdays 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. and 60/65/70 on weekends and legal holidays 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Stationary-equipment limits are 60/65/70 on weekdays and 55/60/65 on weekends and legal holidays. These table windows do not override the more restrictive current construction hours. Engines must be muffled and maintained; unnecessary idling is prohibited; stationary equipment must be placed as far from residences as practical; quiet equipment must be selected where possible; and pile drivers, impulsive sources, and jackhammers are prohibited Sundays and holidays except emergencies or advance approval. At a fixed location, an official warning follows a determined violation; persistence for more than five minutes or recurrence within 90 days is a violation.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit, Conditions of Approval, temporary waiver, project type and number of dwelling units, whether the work is public or emergency work, exact day and start/stop times, preconstruction activity, and every equipment type. For the dBA table, record whether equipment is mobile and used for less than 15 days or stationary, the affected property's zone, measurement location, ambient conditions, and maximum sound. Also document muffling, idling, equipment placement, pile driving, impulsive tools, and any Sunday or holiday approval. Record the official warning and any persistence beyond five minutes or recurrence within 90 days. A phone estimate cannot determine this schedule-, permit-, zone-, equipment-, and measurement-dependent rule by itself.
rules.nextAction: File an ongoing construction-code complaint through Richmond's current iMS system. Code Enforcement is 510-621-1279. For active after-hours construction noise, call Richmond Police non-emergency at 510-233-1214. Include the permit and conditions, project type, waiver, exact activity and time, affected zone, measurements, equipment controls, and warning history.

rules.title: Check the ten-minute or half-hour test
rules.summary: Sunnyvale prohibits an owner or custodian from allowing an animal to bark, bay, cry, howl, or make other noise continuously and incessantly for 10 minutes within any 15-minute period, or intermittently for 30 minutes or more, when it disturbs another person. There is no dB threshold. Whether to issue a citation is left to an animal control officer, police officer, or other safety officer.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address and each start and stop time. State whether the noise was continuous for 10 minutes within a 15-minute window or intermittent for at least 30 minutes, and describe how it disturbed you.
rules.nextAction: Call the Sunnyvale Public Safety desk officer at 408-730-7110 to report barking dogs.

rules.title: Identify the receiving property and source
rules.summary: Sunnyvale operational-noise limits depend on the affected property. Daytime is 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; nighttime is 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. Single-family or duplex property lines: 60 dBA day/50 night. Multifamily primary usable open space: 65/55. Residential property along major transportation corridors or mixed-use residential property: 70/60. Adjacent nonresidential property lines: 70/60; industrial operational noise has a 75 dBA daytime limit. Temporary daytime powered equipment, construction, deliveries, warnings, emergency repairs, street sweeping, and refuse collection have separate rules or exemptions. Loudspeakers or amplifiers projecting sound outdoors are separately barred from 10:00 p.m.–10:00 a.m. unless used for a permitted public event.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source, exact time and duration, affected property's type and location, and the required measurement point: the adjacent single-family/duplex property line or the primary usable open space for the other residential categories. Note whether the source is temporary powered equipment, a delivery, construction, a loudspeaker, an emergency activity, or another listed exception.
rules.nextAction: For noise before 7:00 a.m. or after 10:00 p.m., call Sunnyvale Public Safety non-emergency at 408-730-7180. A written neighborhood complaint can also be submitted through MySunnyvale.

rules.title: Identify owner work and any waiver
rules.summary: Sunnyvale construction is generally allowed Monday–Friday 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. and Saturday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; none is allowed Sunday or on federal holidays when city offices are closed. For a detached single-family home, an owner doing the work with no more than two unpaid helpers may work Monday–Friday 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m., Saturday 8:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m., and Sunday or applicable holidays 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Loud environmentally disruptive noise that is a nuisance remains prohibited. Emergency work may occur at any time, and the chief building official may grant different hours when the added work will not be a nuisance.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, activity, exact start and stop times, day or holiday, and disruptive equipment. Determine whether the property is a detached single-family home and whether the owner plus no more than two unpaid helpers are doing the work. Note any emergency or approved waiver.
rules.nextAction: Submit a written neighborhood or construction complaint through MySunnyvale. For a disturbance needing immediate Public Safety assistance, call 408-730-7180.

rules.title: Check the reasonable-person rule and Animal Services warning-letter process
rules.summary: Santa Rosa City Code § 17-16.110 prohibits keeping or permitting an otherwise lawful animal or fowl whose sound, cry, or behavior causes annoyance or discomfort to a reasonable person of normal sensitiveness in a residential neighborhood. It sets no fixed minute or dB threshold and does not make a preliminary warning part of the violation. Sonoma County Animal Services enforces animal-noise rules for Santa Rosa. Its current process requires the animal's exact street address plus the complainant's name and address; Animal Services then sends the owner a letter stating that allowing an animal to disturb the peace is illegal, offering guidance, and identifying possible consequences. That letter is the agency's initial complaint procedure, not the legal definition of qualifying animal noise. Animal Services says it will not give the complainant's name or contact information to the animal owner, while also warning that public-records law prevents a guarantee that the information will never be disclosed in records.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the animal's exact address, each date, start and stop time, frequency and duration, the sound or behavior, and how it annoyed or caused discomfort to a reasonable person in the residential neighborhood. Preserve audio, video, your Animal Services case information, and any known warning-letter history.
rules.nextAction: Call Sonoma County Animal Services with the animal's exact address and your name and address to start the warning-letter process. Use the official issue page to review the current process and service hours.

rules.title: Check reasonable-person disturbance, zone, time, property line, and amplified-sound rules
rules.summary: Santa Rosa prohibits willfully making or continuing loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise that disturbs neighborhood peace or causes discomfort or annoyance to a reasonable person of normal sensitiveness. The City considers level, intensity, usual or unusual character, natural or unnatural origin, background, sleeping facilities, zoning, population density, time, duration, recurrence, and commercial character. In a residential zone, a radio, musical instrument, television, or similar device may not disturb neighboring residents; exceeding the code's ambient-base level by more than 5 dB at the property line, or inside an adjoining apartment or condominium, is prima facie evidence. For R1/R2 areas, that means more than 50 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., 55 dBA from 7:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m., or 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. For multifamily areas, it means more than 55 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. or 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. A reading at or below those numbers does not prove compliance because the separate reasonable-person test still applies. Sound measurements must use A weighting and slow response on a meter meeting the City's stated standard at the legally relevant property line or adjoining unit. Separate amplified-sound rules generally limit operation to 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; commercial amplified sound is prohibited Sundays and legal holidays, noncommercial amplified sound is allowed 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on those days, and the City Manager may waive the hours. Amplified sound may not exceed the applicable ambient base by 15 dB, operate within 200 feet of a church, school, or hospital, or be unreasonably loud or disturbing. Amplification directed to people on a street, alley, sidewalk, park, or other public property requires Police registration three days beforehand. Chapter 17-16 does not require a preliminary warning before a violation; after notification to desist, each day the violation continues is a separate offense.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address and zone, affected property line or adjoining unit, exact time and duration, recurrence, how it disturbed a reasonable person, and whether sound amplification, a public location, registration, waiver, school, church, or hospital is involved. Preserve audio and video. For supporting measurements, record the A-weighted slow-response meter model, calibration, exact position, and applicable code period.
rules.nextAction: Call Santa Rosa Police Non-Emergency while a party or neighborhood disturbance is active. For a recurring property or equipment violation, submit the City's Code Investigation Request Form; staff generally sends the first inspection notice or owner letter within two weeks.

rules.title: Check zone, time, property-line level, reasonable-person impact, and project conditions
rules.summary: Santa Rosa's citywide noise chapter does not establish one universal construction-hours schedule or a construction-equipment-specific maximum. Individual permits, conditions of approval, and environmental documents may impose project-specific hours or limits and must be checked. Citywide, § 17-16.120 prohibits machinery or equipment noise at a property line more than 5 dB above the code's ambient-base level. The resulting limits are 50 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., 55 dBA from 7:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m., and 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. in R1/R2 areas; 55 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. and 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. in multifamily areas; 60 dBA at night and 65 dBA by day in office/commercial areas; 60 dBA at night and 70 dBA by day in intensive-commercial areas; and 75 dBA at any time in industrial areas. Measurements must use A weighting and slow response on a meter meeting the City's stated standard at the property line. Separately, § 17-16.040 prohibits loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise that disturbs neighborhood peace or annoys a reasonable person, considering level, intensity, character, background, sleeping facilities, zoning, density, time, duration, recurrence, and commercial nature. Therefore, being below the machinery number or working during a project-approved hour does not by itself prove compliance. Chapter 17-16 does not require a preliminary warning before a violation; once notification to desist is given, each day the violation continues is a separate offense. The City's complaint form says the first inspection or owner notification letter is generally sent within two weeks.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address and zone, permit number and conditions, exact activity and equipment, date, start and stop times, duration and recurrence, affected property line, and how the noise disturbed people. Preserve audio and video. For supporting measurements, record A-weighted slow-response level, meter model and calibration, exact property-line position, and applicable time period.
rules.nextAction: Submit the City's exact Code Investigation Request Form. For form questions, call Code Enforcement at 707-543-3198. If a serious disturbing-noise violation is active, call Police Non-Emergency at 707-528-5222.

rules.title: Document disturbing animal noise
rules.summary: Fremont prohibits animal noise that is disturbing, excessive, or offensive. The rule sets no fixed duration or dB threshold. Noise caused by a trespass, threatened trespass, teasing, provocation, or another legitimate cause is excluded. For a barking complaint, first notify the owner. If it continues, Animal Services sends a Barking Log and Petition: track two weeks, obtain signatures from at least two other people who do not live at the same address, and return it within seven days after the tracking period.
rules.captureInstruction: Record every date, start and end time, duration, source address, and how the barking affected you. Note any apparent trespass, threat, teasing, provocation, or other cause. Complete the city's two-week log and obtain the two required outside-household signatures.
rules.nextAction: Notify the dog owner first. If the barking continues, submit the official form or call Animal Services at 510-790-6635. Return the Barking Log and Petition within seven days after the two-week tracking period.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Report a Barking Dog - City of Fremont

rules.title: Document unreasonable noise at any hour
rules.summary: Fremont has no fixed citywide dB cutoff for general noise. At any hour, loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise may violate the rule when it disturbs a neighborhood or a reasonable person; the city considers the sound and background levels, proximity to sleeping areas, zoning, density, time, duration, repetition, and whether the activity is commercial. Between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., music or electronics plainly audible 50 feet from its building, structure, or vehicle is prima facie evidence of a violation. The 50-foot test is distance, not 50 dB. Emergencies and specified permitted or daytime activities are exempt.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the exact time, duration, repetition, source and affected locations, background conditions, and how the noise disturbed you. At night, document whether it was plainly audible from 50 feet away. Also note any permit, emergency, authorized event, residential maintenance, or other apparent exemption.
rules.nextAction: For an active or non-urgent disturbance needing an officer, call Fremont Police non-emergency dispatch at 510-790-6800 and select option 3.

rules.title: Identify the project before checking hours
rules.summary: Fremont construction hours depend on the project. Development projects within 500 feet of a residence, lodging facility, nursing home, or inpatient hospital: weekdays 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.; Saturdays and holidays 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; no Sundays. Development projects farther than 500 feet: weekdays 6:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; weekends and holidays 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Resident homeowners and unpaid volunteers working on their own detached single-family home: weekdays 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; weekends 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Emergency work is excluded, and a city-approved project may have modified hours shown on its plans or notice board.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the address, activity, exact start and end times, day or holiday, and distance to the nearest residence, lodging facility, nursing home, or inpatient hospital. Identify whether it is a development project or a resident homeowner with unpaid volunteers. Photograph posted permit hours or the notice board and note any emergency or city-approved modification.
rules.nextAction: If the work is outside the schedule that applies to that project, submit a Fremont App service request under Building and Construction (In Progress).

rules.title: Check the continuous 10-minute rule and staged warning process
rules.summary: San Francisco defines a barking dog as one that barks, bays, cries, howls, or makes other noise continuously and incessantly for 10 minutes to the disturbance of another person. There is no dB threshold. It is not a violation while someone is trespassing or threatening to trespass, or while someone is teasing or provoking the dog. Under Health Code § 41.12(e), two unrelated people living in different households within 300 feet who are disturbed may sign affidavits and ask a police officer to cite the owner or guardian. The City's current complaint process starts by calling 311: 311 records the complaint, and Animal Care and Control and Police issue warning letters for the first two complaints. If the problem continues, the complainant may go to a local police station with a neighbor to file a report that may trigger a citation. Police ordinarily do not dispatch solely for barking without a public-safety threat or animal-endangerment issue.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the exact dog address, start and stop times proving 10 uninterrupted minutes, every break in barking, what disturbance it caused, whether trespass or provocation was involved, 311 case numbers and warning history, and contact information for a second unrelated household within 300 feet if seeking a citation.
rules.nextAction: Call 311 with the dog's exact address to create the complaint record and begin the City's warning-letter process. After the first two complaints, take a neighbor from a different household within 300 feet to a local police station if the qualifying barking continues.
rules.officialSourceLabel: San Francisco Health Code §§ 41 and 41.12 / City Barking-Dog Procedure

rules.title: Check disturbance, distance, source property, ambient, permit, and measurement
rules.summary: Police Code § 49 prohibits a radio, television, musical instrument, sound system, or similar device that produces raucous noise, disturbs neighborhood peace and comfort, or is louder than necessary. Between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., plainly audible sound 50 feet from the source property's boundary is prima facie evidence of a violation; exceeding Article 29 at any time is also prima facie evidence. Article 29 limits machine, device, music, or entertainment noise from residential property to 5 dBA above ambient outside its property plane, and on the same multi-unit residential property to 5 dBA above ambient three feet from another unit's wall, floor, or ceiling with its windows and doors closed. Commercial or industrial source property uses 8 dBA above ambient outside its property plane; regulated entertainment also has an 8 dBC low-frequency test. Public-property equipment uses 10 dBA above ambient at 25 feet or more. A fixed source inside a residential sleeping or living room is limited to 45 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. and 55 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m., measured with windows open unless mechanical ventilation lets them remain closed. A City permit with different noise limits controls, and an agency may grant a variance. The legal tests use a Type 1 precision meter: at least 10 minutes of ambient with the source silent and at least one minute for the source, plus prescribed outdoor or indoor microphone positions. Neither § 49 nor Article 29 requires a preliminary warning before a violation. A phone's maximum reading by itself cannot decide these tests.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address and property type, exact time, how it disturbed people, whether it was plainly audible 50 feet beyond the source property after 10:00 p.m., and any permit. Preserve audio and video. For supporting measurements, document at least one minute with the source and 10 minutes of ambient with it silent, the property plane or interior position, distance, doors and windows, meter type, and calibration.
rules.nextAction: Call Police Non-Emergency while an unreasonable neighbor or party disturbance is in progress. Use the City's exact noise form for equipment, businesses, permitted entertainment, and other listed noise sources.
rules.officialSourceLabel: San Francisco Police Code § 49 and Article 29

rules.title: Check equipment, distance, night permit, emergency, and official measurement
rules.summary: Police Code § 2907 prohibits powered construction equipment above 80 dBA at 100 feet, or the equivalent level at another convenient distance. That limit does not apply to impact tools that have approved intake and exhaust mufflers and, for pavement breakers and jackhammers, approved acoustic shields or shrouds; emergency work is also exempt. Construction helicopters are separately limited to two hours in one day and four hours in one week. Section 2908 prohibits building or structure construction, demolition, excavation, alteration, or repair from 8:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. when it exceeds ambient by 5 dBA at the nearest property plane, unless Public Works or Building Inspection granted a special permit; emergency work is exempt. The City describes 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. work as generally permitted, but daytime timing alone does not satisfy the equipment limit, permit conditions, or a variance. The legal tests use a Type 1 precision meter, at least one minute for source noise, at least 10 minutes of ambient with the source silent, and prescribed microphone placement. Article 29 does not require a preliminary warning before a construction violation. Building Inspection enforces private-property work; Public Works enforces publicly owned work. A phone's maximum reading and elapsed time alone cannot establish compliance or violation.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the address, whether the work is private or public, equipment type, actual equipment-to-microphone distance, date and time, permit and special-night-permit details, and any claimed emergency. Preserve audio and video. For supporting measurements, document a one-minute source level, a 10-minute ambient level with the source silent at the nearest property plane for night work, microphone position, meter type, and calibration.
rules.nextAction: Use the City's exact noise form for private- or public-property construction. For qualifying nighttime work in progress without a special permit, call Police Non-Emergency.
rules.officialSourceLabel: San Francisco Police Code Article 29 §§ 2901–2908 and 2916
rules.secondaryActionLabel: Call Police for Active Night Work

rules.title: Check habitual or nuisance barking and the five-person abatement route
rules.summary: Daly City prohibits an owner or caretaker from permitting an animal to habitually bark, meow, disturb a citizen's peace, or become a public nuisance. It separately declares excessive, continuous, or untimely barking to be a nuisance. Neither rule sets a fixed minute or dB threshold. A separate abatement procedure applies when five or more people with separate residences, or five or more people regularly employed in the neighborhood, affirm in writing that the animal is an habitual nuisance; if the poundmaster finds the nuisance exists, the owner or custodian is served notice to abate it. The five-person requirement belongs to that abatement route and is not the definition of every animal-noise violation. An animal-control, humane, or peace officer may issue an administrative citation after determining that the animal-control chapter was violated; the chapter does not require a warning before every citation. Peninsula Humane Society states that it is not contracted to handle barking complaints and that each city handles them itself.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the animal address, every date, start and stop time, breaks, frequency, whether the barking was excessive, continuous, habitual, or untimely, and exactly how it disturbed the peace. For the formal abatement route, preserve signed written statements and addresses or neighborhood workplaces for five separate people.
rules.nextAction: Call the Daly City Police Department non-emergency front desk for the City's barking process and ask where to submit the written statements if using the five-person abatement route. Do not route a barking-only complaint to Peninsula Humane Society.

rules.title: Check public-peace disturbance, nighttime audibility, and amplifier permit
rules.summary: Daly City Municipal Code § 9.22.010 prohibits making, or allowing on premises under one's control, any noise, disorder, or tumult that disturbs the public peace at any time. Section 9.22.030 separately prohibits, from 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m., causing or allowing noise, music, sound, or another disturbance on one's property that may be heard by, disturbs, or harasses another person beyond the property, quarters, or apartment where it originates. No minute or dB threshold appears in these sections. A loudspeaker or sound amplifier projecting sound outside a building or outdoors requires a written Police Chief permit stating the permittee, purpose, authorized time and place, and termination date. Chapter 9.22 does not require a preliminary warning before a violation. A phone reading or the clock alone cannot decide whether the required audibility or disturbance exists or whether a permit applies.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact start and stop times, whether it could be heard beyond the source property, quarters, or apartment, whom it disturbed or harassed, and whether an outdoor loudspeaker or amplifier and Police Chief permit were involved. Preserve audio and video from the affected location.
rules.nextAction: For an active disturbance, call Daly City Police 24-hour direct dispatch. For a recurring private-property nuisance that is no longer active, use the City's current iHelp page.

rules.title: Apply the new 2026 hours, daylight-saving schedule, equipment rule, and exemption
rules.summary: Daly City's new Chapter 15.09 applies to outdoor work on private property for a project requiring a building permit. During standard time, work is limited to 8:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. Monday–Friday and 9:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. Saturday and Sunday. During daylight-saving time, the same start times apply but work may continue until 8:30 p.m. Construction is prohibited on federal holidays unless the Building Official or designee grants an exemption. Deliveries of materials or equipment are not allowed outside the applicable hours. Staging and site preparation may begin up to one hour before the start time only if no construction equipment is used; equipment use outside the applicable hours is strictly prohibited. During permitted hours, § 15.09.020 incorporates the temporary construction-noise levels in the General Plan Noise Element. That document identifies earthmoving equipment at 70–95 dBA at 50 feet, impact equipment at 80–105 dBA at 50 feet, and pile driving up to 105 dBA at 50 feet; the chapter does not create one universal phone-meter cutoff for every equipment type and project condition. Required hour signs must be five feet above ground and visible at every construction entrance. A written exemption may be granted for an emergency or exceptional circumstances beyond the applicant's control, must be posted, and may be revoked. Enforcement may include a warning notice, an inspection hold, or a stop-work order; a warning is a possible enforcement action, not a mandatory prerequisite. The general 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m. disturbing-noise rule still applies where relevant.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the address, whether work is outdoors on private property and requires a building permit, date, daylight-saving or standard time, activity and equipment, deliveries or staging, exact start and stop times, distance from the equipment, posted-hours sign, permit conditions, and any posted exemption. Preserve audio, video, and readings from a documented position.
rules.nextAction: Report the construction violation to Code Enforcement through Daly City iHelp, email codeenforcement@dalycity.org, or call 650-991-8260. For a disturbing violation actively occurring during the 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m. police-noise period, call 24-hour dispatch at 650-992-1225.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Daly City Municipal Code Chapter 15.09 / Official Construction Hours Handout

rules.title: Document frequent or extended barking
rules.summary: Santa Clara prohibits keeping a dog whose loud barking or unusual noises disturb the peace and quiet of one or more people in the immediate neighborhood. Loud barking means barking, howling, or baying by day or night for frequent and/or extended periods that becomes a nuisance and prevents comfortable enjoyment of a home. The rule sets no fixed minute or dB threshold. Barking while the dog is protecting against or resisting a trespasser is excluded; the owner bears the burden of proving that exception.
rules.captureInstruction: Record each date, start and stop time, frequency, duration, source address, and how the noise prevented comfortable enjoyment of your home. Note any apparent trespass or protective response.
rules.nextAction: First try a neighborly request when safe. If habitual barking continues, report it while it is happening to Santa Clara Police/Public Safety Dispatch at 408-615-5580.

rules.title: Separate fixed-source and conduct rules
rules.summary: Santa Clara's numeric limits apply only to fixed sources and are measured on affected property. Residential receiving zones: 55 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. and 50 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; commercial/office: 65/60; light industrial: 70 at any time; heavy industrial: 75. Music or informational speech reduces the applicable limit by 5 dBA, while a different ambient level can adjust it in 5 dBA steps. The chapter does not cover mobile sources. Separately, California Penal Code § 415(2) covers malicious and willful loud, unreasonable disturbance. Emergencies, permitted outdoor events, allowed-hours construction, and other listed activities are exempt from the fixed-source chapter.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source, exact time, duration, repetition, affected property's zoning, closest measurement point on affected property, and a background reading. Identify whether the source was fixed or mobile and whether it contained music or speech. Note any emergency, permit, event, or other apparent exemption. A phone estimate is supporting evidence and is not the code-specified sound-level-meter measurement.
rules.nextAction: Report a violation in progress to Santa Clara Police non-emergency at 408-615-5580. For questions or a later discussion with an officer, call the front desk at 408-615-4700 between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Santa Clara City Code Chapter 9.10, Article I

rules.title: Check distance, work type, and exemptions
rules.summary: On a privately owned construction site within 300 feet of residentially zoned property, Santa Clara allows building, related road or walkway, pool, landscape work, related operations, and material deliveries only Monday–Friday 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. and non-holiday Saturdays 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. No such work is permitted Sundays or on the holidays listed in § 9.10.230. Exemptions include emergency protection of life or property, state-preempted work such as public-school construction, utility service work, public inspections, and work an owner performs on an existing single-family or duplex home.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, exact activity or delivery, start and stop times, day or holiday, and distance to residentially zoned property. Identify whether the owner is personally working on an existing single-family or duplex home, or whether the work is emergency, utility, public inspection, public-school, or otherwise state-preempted.
rules.nextAction: For a violation in progress, call Santa Clara Police non-emergency at 408-615-5580. Submit a written request through MySantaClara when immediate response is unnecessary.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Santa Clara City Code Chapter 9.10, Article II
